product-owner.name: Product Owner
product-owner.responsibility: Final say on product direction, priorities, business trade-offs, and experiment verdicts
does_not: make architectural calls without consulting architect

product-manager.name: Product Manager
product-manager.responsibility: Owns refinement; turns raw issues into ready tickets that developers can safely pick up
does_not: decide architecture, UX, or security questions
self-refine bounced-back issues without addressing the specific gap

architect.name: Architect
architect.responsibility: Owns architecture, reliability, performance, and cost decisions
does_not: implement feature tickets (though they implement spike investigations)

designer.name: Designer
designer.responsibility: Owns user flows, accessibility, and design-system contributions

security.name: Security Engineer
security.responsibility: Owns authentication, secrets, PII, threat modeling, and supply-chain concerns
does_not: decide architecture (beyond security implications) or UX questions

developer.name: Developer
developer.responsibility: Implements changes end-to-end: code, tests, PR, merge

peer-reviewer.name: Peer Reviewer
peer-reviewer.responsibility: Reviews PRs for design, intent, readability, and risk

tester.name: Tester
tester.responsibility: Verifies PRs behaviorally on preview environments
does_not: fix the bug they found (report only)
approve on the basis of 'the code looks fine'

release-manager.name: Release Manager
release-manager.responsibility: Owns release mechanics: cadence, cut, release notes, RC tagging, deploy coordination
does_not: decide what's in the release (that's pm)
give the go/no-go (that's product-owner or incident-commander for patch trains)

incident-commander.name: Incident Commander
incident-commander.responsibility: Owns the incident lifecycle: triage, coordination, communication, postmortem creation
does_not: draft or own the postmortem (that's pm)

incident-responder.name: Incident Responder
incident-responder.responsibility: Owns incident diagnosis and mitigation execution: root-cause investigation, rollback/toggle/hotfix
does_not: decide mitigation strategy (recommends to IC, IC decides)
draft or own the postmortem (that's pm; responder contributes root-cause findings)
